item.description:
A polish pass on the panel.
- Scrolling the panel is smooth. It used to stall whenever the pointer was between two cards. - Sliders now snap to steps, with a tick at each, so a setting is easy to return to. - Cards have more room, hairlines between rows and clearer icons, and buttons respond to the pointer. - Clicking the space between cards closes the panel.

The first version of Lull. It blurs everything on screen except the window you are working in.
### Focus
- Lull follows the window in front, whether you switch with the pointer or the keyboard. - App-wide focus keeps every window of the app in front sharp. - App groups keep chosen apps sharp together. - Ignored apps make Lull stand down while they are in front. Finder is ignored to begin with. - With more than one display, choose one focus across all of them or one per screen. - Stage Manager's thumbnails stay sharp, unless you turn on Blur Stage Manager.
### Look
- Two modes: Ambient keeps the top of the screen clear and fades to full blur about halfway down; Deep blurs everything. - Sliders for blur, tint and grain, with a tint colour of your choice. - Monochrome drains the colour from everything that is blurred. - Set how fast the blur arrives, and how: Fade, Focus or Pointer.
### Control
- A panel opens from the menu bar icon. - Shake the pointer to turn Lull on or off. Hold Shift and shake to peek at everything. - Peek at corners, if you turn it on, shows everything while the pointer rests in a screen corner. - Four keyboard shortcuts: Control-Option-Command with F to toggle Lull, M to switch mode, E to ignore the app in front and C to open the panel. Each can be changed or removed. - Auto-hide tucks away the Dock, the menu bar or both while Lull is focusing. - The `lull` command and `lull://` links control everything from scripts. Install the command from Scripting Commands in the panel.
### Good to know
- Lull needs macOS 26 or later. - It needs no permissions for normal use. Only Auto-hide asks for Automation, and only when you turn it on. - Lull starts at login, checks for updates once a day and installs an update the next time it quits. Both can be turned off in the panel.
